dedupe_keys.name: global maps of suitability and potential for agricultural expansion at 300 m cengic et al 2019 2020 and 2023 releases

description: Global rasters of the potential for land to be converted to agriculture, for three categories taken from ESA CCI land cover: cropland only (rainfed and irrigated merged), mosaics with more than 50 percent crops, and mosaics with less than 50 percent crops. The 2023 Zenodo release says artificial neural network models related conversions recorded from 2007 to 2020 to topography, climate, soil and accessibility, with cross-validation AUC of 0.88 to 0.93 and hindcast AUC of 0.83 to 0.91 for 1992 to 2006, and that the maps can downscale projections of global land change models. It holds 40 downloadable GeoTIFF files, about 38.5 GB in total, at 10 arc-seconds (about 300 m) with aggregated 30 arc-second and 10 arc-minute layers, free under CC BY 4.0. Two earlier DANS releases (2019 and 2020) hold the first suitability maps, built from 26 IMAGE regions and conversions from 2003 to 2013; no licence is shown in their DataCite metadata. Coverage is global land. Caveats: maps assume past drivers of expansion hold, and suitability is not a forecast. For simulation they place future cropland growth on the grid, to project new demand for rural roads, irrigation water and power, and land conflicts with infrastructure. Related catalogue records include LS-500 global cropland suitability and the cropland expansion pressure dataset to 2030.
